body.p: This is a full and timely response to the outstanding non-final Office Action electronically delivered on August 27, 2024.
Claims 1 and 6 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Inomata et al., (JP 2019102695).
Claims 2-5 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Inomata in view of Kimura et al., (US 20130178979). Description of Amendments
Applicant, after carefully considering the remarks set forth in the Office Action, has amended claims 1 and 6 to incorporate features of claim 2.
Accordingly, claim 2 has been cancelled, and dependencies of claims 3 and 5 have been adapted.

Applicant respectfully submits that the amendments are all premised upon the original disclosure and thus no new matter has been introduced. Applicant respectfully submits that the presently pending claims are in condition for allowance. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the claim rejections are respectfully requested. Discussion of Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 & 103
Claims 2-5 are rejected under 35 US.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Inomata in
view of Kimura et al., (US 20130178979).
Regarding independent claim 1, as currently amended, it recites:
1. An industrial robot for transporting a transported object, comprising:
wherein as viewed in the up-down direction, when a rotation center of the first

hand to the arm coincides with a rotation center of the second hand to the arm and when a rotation angle of the first hand to the arm is equal to a rotation angle of the second hand to the arm, the transported object mounted on the first hand is overlapped
with the transported object mounted on the second hand in the up-down direction,
at the time of execution of the teaching step, a dummy transported object
provided in a shape identical to that of the transported object or the transported object
is already placed in the predetermined position, and
in response to the transported object or the dummy transported object placed in
the predetermined position being a transported object for teaching,
in the teaching step, a position in the up-down direction of the transported

object for teaching placed in the predetermined position is detected by a first sensor attached to the first hand and a position in the horizontal direction of the transported object for teaching placed in the predetermined position is detected by a second sensor attached to the first hand, and the controller identifies and learns the hand position based on detection results by the first sensor and the
second sensor, and
in the calibration step, the second hand is moved to the hand position

identified in the teaching step and the transported object for teaching placed in the predetermined position is mounted and taken out onto the second hand, thereafter, the second hand is moved again to the hand position identified in the teaching step and the transported object for teaching is placed on the placing section, and then the position in the horizontal direction of the transported object for teaching placed on the placing section is detected by the second sensor attached to the first hand, and the controller corrects, based on a detection result by the second sensor, the position in the horizontal direction of the hand position
learned in the teaching step.
(Emphasis added for visual aid)
Applicant respectfully submits that features highlighted in amended claim 1 above are
non-obvious and patentable over the cited references of record. The reasons that support the
above position of Applicant are discussed in detail hereafter.

In rejecting the features as highlighted above (i.e. features of claim 2), the Examiner indicated Inomata does not explicitly teach that it is the second hand that is moved or that the object is placed on the second hand, but Kimura teaches the claimed features.

The Examiner further indicated Kim ura discloses "the hand 10 is controlled so as to travel at 'high speed' for a zone from the teach point a to the teach point c", which teaches the features "the second hand is moved to the hand position identified in the teaching step" in amended claim 1; and discloses "hand 10 is controlled so as to travel at 'low speed' for a zone from the teach point c to the teach point e", which teaches the features "the second hand is moved again to the hand position identified in the teaching step" in amended claim 1.

However, Kim ura actually discloses in paragraph [0089] that "if the wafer W is absent both in the first hand l0a and the second hand lOb at the teach point a (specifically, for pattern # 1 of FIG. 5B), the hand 10 is controlled so as to travel at "high speed" for a zone from the teach point a to the teach point c", and discloses in paragraph [0090] that "if the wafer W is obtained ("GET") by the second hand 10b at the teach point c under the condition (specifically, for pattern # 3 in FIG. 5B), the hand 10 is controlled so as to travel at "low speed" for a zone from the teach point c to the teach point e".

Applicant respectfully submits that the above disclosure of Kimura merely teaches controlling the hand 10 to travel at "high speed" or "low speed" based on "whether the wafer W is obtained ("GET") by the second hand 10b" without teaching or suggesting "detection of the position of the transported object for teaching" and "correction of hand position", and therefore fails to teach or disclose the features "the second hand is moved to the hand position identified in the teaching step and the transported object for teaching placed in the predetermined position is mounted and taken out onto the second hand", thereafter, "the

second hand is moved again to the hand position identified in the teaching step and the transported object for teaching is placed on the placing section", and then "the position in the horizontal direction of the transported object for teaching placed on the placing section is detected by the second sensor attached to the first hand, and the controller corrects, based on a detection result by the second sensor, the position in the horizontal direction of the hand position learned in the teaching step" as recited in amended claim 1.

Based on the above, it is submitted persons skilled in the art, from teaching of Inomata, Kim ura and other cited references would not arrive at the present invention as claimed in the amended claim 1 by using or combining the knowledge of the references without being inventive. Therefore, claim 1, as currently amended, should be novel, non-obvious and patentable over Inomata and Kim ura. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections on claim 1 is respectfully requested.

Regarding dependent claims 3-5, these dependent claims should overcome the rejections as a matter of law, for at least the reasons that these dependent claims contain all features of the independent claim 1.

Regarding independent claim 6, for the same reasons set forth above of claim 1, claim 6 which disclose corresponding technical features should be also novel, non-obvious and patentable over the cited references, and withdrawal of the rejections on claim 6 is respectfully requested.
For at least the foregoing reasons, it is believed that all pending claims are in proper
condition for allowance and an action to such effect is earnestly solicited. If the Examiner
believes that a telephone conference would expedite the examination of the above-identified
patent application, the Examiner is invited to call the undersigned.
Respectfully submitted,
